description: SECURITY (s440 fix round, F3). A `let inner = 5` inside a sibling block `if (true) { … }` is visible only inside that block; the `.some` callback outside it calls the nested async helper `inner` (which calls a server fn). The server answers false for every element, so the verdict MUST be "rejected". Treating the sibling-block `let` as a function-scope binding hid the helper's asyncness: `.some` received an always-truthy Promise per element and answered "accepted" for every input.
rationale: §13.2: every server call site is awaited, and any function containing a server call is async. Lexical block scope decides that `inner(x)` names the nested helper (not the block-local `let`), so the helper's calls are server call sites; the `.some` callback is lifted to an awaited combinator and the server's answer decides the verdict.
